en: The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
Volcanic ash from Mount Mayon weathers into nutrient-rich soil that is excellent for growing abaca plants.
Surigao del Norte contains large laterite nickel deposits that are mined to make stainless steel and batteries.
The Angat Dam in Bulacan collects rainwater from the Sierra Madre mountains to supply drinking water to Metro Manila.
Because the Philippines is near the equator, Earth's tilt creates distinct wet and dry seasons instead of four temperate seasons.
Traditional Filipino farmers used the Balatik constellation, part of Ursa Major, to know when to plant rice.
Fishermen in Manila Bay catch more fish during spring tides, which occur during the full and new moon.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released massive amounts of ash and gas that temporarily cooled global temperatures.
The Philippine Fault System is a 1,250-kilometer tectonic fault line that can cause major earthquakes across the archipelago.
Super Typhoon Yolanda in 2013 generated a massive storm surge that severely flooded the coastal city of Tacloban.
The high-quality marble deposits in Cebu are metamorphic rocks originally formed from ancient marine limestone.
During an El Niño event, the Philippines experiences below-average rainfall, which often causes severe droughts and water shortages.
